title: Channapatna lacquered toys
summary: Channapatna, in Karnataka, is known as the toy town of India. Craftspeople turn soft wood on a hand lathe and colour it by holding sticks of lac against the spinning piece. Here you turn the shape of a toy top, then melt on its bright bands.
howToPlay: Look at the lit toy at the top: it shows the shape and the colour of each band.
Drag across the spinning wood to set how wide each row is turned.
Tap a band, then tap a lac colour to melt it on.
Press Check to see your stars.
rules: The toy is turned in ten rows; the shape counts for most of the score.
Each band should carry the lac colour shown on the toy.
The wood is raw until a band is glazed; a band you leave bare scores nothing.
Reshape starts the wood again; undo takes back the last change.
Three stars for a clean shape with every band in the right colour.
heritageNote: Toys have been turned in Channapatna for more than two centuries. Makers use local soft wood and colour it with natural lac dyes: the friction of the spinning piece melts the stick into a smooth, glossy band. The craft is protected as a geographical indication of India.
